points.quote: AI tools must only be used when the assessment instructions permit its use.’ Where AI is used to generate content, it must be referenced as a source.
points.gist: AI tools must only be used when assessment instructions permit it, and AI-generated content must be referenced as a source.

points.quote: Students and staﬀ are not permitted to upload student assessments or any identiﬁable data to AI applications for any reason (this includes attempts to check for AI generated content).
points.gist: Students and staff may not upload student assessments or identifiable data to AI applications for any reason, including checking for AI-generated content.

points.quote: Students who submit work generated by AI, but pass it oﬀ as their own, will have committed academic misconduct.
points.gist: Students who submit AI-generated work and pass it off as their own will have committed academic misconduct.

points.quote: it is up to the course team to decide what constitutes acceptable use, which may be negotiated by assignment or as an overall principle.
points.gist: The course team decides what counts as acceptable AI use, which may be negotiated by assignment or as an overall principle.

points.quote: Staﬀ and students may not upload any content access through University-subscribed resources, including Library resources, to LLMs as this will potentially breach licence and copyright restrictions.
points.gist: Staff and students may not upload content accessed through University-subscribed resources, including Library resources, to LLMs, as this may breach licence and copyright restrictions.

points.quote: Students should not be required to use a speciﬁc AI tool in any assignment due to inequitable access to these tools.
points.gist: Students should not be required to use a specific AI tool in any assignment because access to such tools is unequal.

points.quote: AI tools may not be used to analyse primary data, particularly where it involves human participants (whether collected directly or user generated), unless this is explicitly stated in the relevant ethics application.
points.gist: AI tools may not be used to analyse primary data, especially involving human participants, unless the relevant ethics application explicitly states this.

points.quote: Students hold the copyright for all works created during their studies.
points.gist: Students hold the copyright for all works created during their studies.

points.quote: This therefore excludes the use of AI tools from marking and giving feedback.
points.gist: Because students own copyright in their work, AI tools are excluded from marking and giving feedback.

points.quote: Avoid a blanket reliance on AI detection tools, as they are (currently) highly inaccurate and underscore the biases inherent in them.
points.gist: Avoid blanket reliance on AI detection tools, as they are currently highly inaccurate and underscore inherent biases.

points.quote: Running the assessment brief through ChatGPT or Co-pilot to see if AI produces a work that would pass. If so, the assessment should be redeveloped so it cannot.
points.gist: Staff may run the assessment brief through ChatGPT or Co-pilot; if AI produces a passing work, the assessment should be redeveloped.

points.quote: Requiring a list of process steps, with reﬂections on what tools the students have used to complete their work, what they could have done diﬀerently and why.
points.gist: Staff may require a list of process steps with reflections on tools used, what could have been done differently and why.

points.quote: Open discussions about speciﬁc cases and challenges should be encouraged without the fear of facing penalties.
points.gist: Open discussions about specific cases and challenges should be encouraged without fear of penalties.

points.quote: use of the latter may not necessarily constitute academic misconduct.
points.gist: Use of language support or translation tools may not necessarily constitute academic misconduct.

points.quote: one GPT query uses over 1500% more energy than a single Google search; Google’s AI alone consumes the same amount of energy in a year as Ireland
points.gist: One GPT query uses over 1500% more energy than a Google search, and Google's AI alone uses as much energy yearly as Ireland.
